---
title: "Start Here"
---

Agent Odyssey is a short role-playing course on using coding agents (LLM tools that read and run code for you) safely in bioinformatics work. You need no LLM experience, and nothing here asks you to use these tools. It shows how to use them with care if you choose to.

## How it works

- **Walk the trunk.** It is <span data-ao-n="trunk">14</span> quests in order, from fears and kinds of machine to your first agent and trust in output. The Wall of Output ends it.
- **Pick branches.** Each branch is a topic you can take when it matches your work. Quests marked side quest are optional.
- **Clear the Murk.** The final boss opens after the whole trunk and any <span data-ao-n="any">3</span> of the <span data-ao-n="branches">8</span> branches.
- **Save your progress.** It lives in this browser. **Save code** in the top bar copies a code, and **Load code** restores it elsewhere.

The trunk takes about three hours and each branch one to two more. The order is advice, and every quest stays open.

## Keep exploring

This course covers a small part of what these tools can do. The [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) are the best place to learn more, and each quest's Lore section links the pages that matter for it. Browse the overview whenever you are curious.

For research-specific guidance, [AI for Science](https://aiforscience.eu/) collects draft best practices for agentic AI in science from European task forces and institutions, and has a one-page [short version](https://aiforscience.eu/short-version/). The practices are drafts with no endorsements yet, and several are written for institutions and funders. Nine quests draw on one practice each: Three Kinds of Machine, Advice or Enforcement, Secrets and Sensitive Ground, Close the Loop, Ground Truth, Plug In a Server, Guard the Door, the Wall of Output and The Project Charter.
